answer: Final synthesis: The down-regulated gene sets are definitively established — 91 genes (GluFevsGluFePlus) and 289 genes (SuccvsGluFePlus) at log2FC ≤ −1.5 and padj ≤ 0.05, out of 5828 measured PA14 genes (contrasts "Media MMGluFeMinus vs MMGluFePlus" and "Media Succinate vs MMGluFePlus"; both RDS inputs parsed directly). The enrichKEGG-equivalent ORA pipeline (per-condition one-sided hypergeometric/Fisher exact → BH padj ≤ 0.05, min pathway size 10, map-level pathways, measured-gene background, ID-intersection of the two conditions) is fully implemented in kegg_ora_analysis.py and its math was executed and validated on clearly-labeled synthetic snapshots (fisher-exact p == 1 − hypergeom.cdf(k−1) verified; BH; minGSSize; two-condition intersection). The number of common pathways is NOT COMPUTABLE IN THIS ENVIRONMENT (KEGG db unreachable): a final exhaustive sweep confirmed no network (DNS fails for rest.kegg.jp/www.kegg.jp and all hosts; even private IPs are "Network is unreachable") and no KEGG pathway→gene map anywhere on disk (no R/BioConductor/orgDb/KEGG.db, no gseapy/MSigDB, no *.gmt/*.kgml/*.sqlite/*.tsv bundles, no pip cache, whole-filesystem content grep for pathway signatures returns only my own script). Therefore NO numeric pathway count is claimed and none is fabricated. Exact reproduction command to obtain the real count where network is available: `curl -s "https://rest.kegg.jp/link/pathway/pau" > kegg_pau_links.tsv && python3 kegg_ora_analysis.py` → read `common_pathways_count` in `kegg_ora_report.json` (organism 'pau' = UCBPP-PA14, matching the PA14_xxxxx IDs; fallback 'pae'/PAO1 requires lossy orthology mapping).
